proved_step: statement: DNF transition upper bound with shared literals. Let k,q be integers with k>=1 and q>=1. Every function f:{0,1}^k->{0,1}^q has a NOT/AND/OR circuit of size at most q(2^k(k+1)+1), with binary AND/OR gates, shared input negations, and zero-cost constant outputs. Proof: For an output true on r input rows, use the OR of those r minterms. The input negations cost at most k gates total and each minterm uses k-1 AND gates; combining r terms uses r-1 OR gates. Constant outputs cost zero. For nonconstant outputs, the count is at most k+r(k-1)+(r-1) <= k+2^k(k-1)+2^k-1 <= 2^k(k+1)+1. Summing this per-output bound proves the claim. In a circuit convention without free constants, constant outputs require separate treatment.

statement: Conflict-graph state lower bound for full-search streaming. Let F be a set of distinct N-bit truth tables. At cut t, let P_t be the length-t prefixes of members of F, and form H_t on P_t by joining distinct p,q when some suffix u has pu,qu in F. In any deterministic streaming system whose final decoder outputs a circuit computing its input word for every member of F, adjacent prefixes reach distinct states. Therefore the state assignment is a proper coloring of H_t, so the system has at least chi(H_t) states at cut t and at least ceil(log2 chi(H_t)) state bits. Proof: suppose adjacent p,q reach the same state, and choose a common accepting suffix u. Determinism makes the final states after pu and qu equal, so the decoder outputs the same circuit on both. Correctness requires that circuit to compute both distinct truth tables, which is impossible. Thus adjacent vertices have different states. A proper coloring of H_t needs at least chi(H_t) colors, and S bits encode at most 2^S states, giving 2^S >= chi(H_t). This bounds state count only; it does not bound transition-circuit gate cost.

proved_step: statement: Decoder-capacity lower bound (conditional on D being decoder-output bits). Let F be a finite set of M distinct truth tables, and suppose a deterministic full-search streaming machine has a decoder whose output is encoded by D bits and identifies the exact truth table f on every f in F. Then D >= ceil(log2 M). Proof: correctness requires distinct decoder outputs for distinct truth tables, since one output cannot identify two different truth tables. Thus the decoder takes at least M distinct values on reachable final states. Its D-bit output has at most 2^D values, so 2^D >= M and D >= ceil(log2 M). The argument is independent of transition encoding and update-circuit cost. It constrains a fixed (S,G_max,D) frame only when D counts bits that bound the number of distinguishable decoded truth tables; it does not establish an optimal Pareto point.

proved_step: statement: Exact characteristic-vector residual update for membership streaming. Let F⊆{0,1}^N. At cut t, encode a prefix p by the characteristic vector z_p∈{0,1}^{2^{N−t}} of R_t(p)={u∈{0,1}^{N−t}:pu∈F}, with coordinates indexed by suffixes u. For t<N, on input bit b, the next state has coordinates z'_{v}=(¬b∧z_{0v})∨(b∧z_{1v}) for every v∈{0,1}^{N−t−1}. Thus the update is realizable with one shared NOT gate for b and at most 3·2^{N−t−1} AND/OR gates. The terminal state decides membership by testing its sole coordinate. Proof: By definition, R_{t+1}(pb)={v:bv∈R_t(p)}. Its v-coordinate is therefore z_p[bv], which equals z_{0v} if b=0 and z_{1v} if b=1. The displayed Boolean multiplexer computes exactly this coordinate; each uses two AND gates and one OR gate, with ¬b shared. At t=N the residual is {ε} for members and empty for nonmembers, so the final bit is the membership answer. Scope: a time-varying, exponentially wide representation for decision streaming; it gives no fixed-(S,D) Pareto result and no full-search decoder bound.

statement: Per-cut conflict-graph characterization of full-search state assignments. Fix a finite family F subset {0,1}^N and a cut t. Let P_t={p in {0,1}^t: there exists u in {0,1}^{N-t} with pu in F}. Form the graph H_t on P_t, joining distinct p,q exactly when there is a suffix u with pu and qu both in F. Any deterministic streaming system whose final decoder returns the input truth table on every member of F assigns different states to adjacent vertices of H_t. Consequently its number of states is at least chi(H_t), and at least chi(H_t)+1 if it must also assign every dead prefix a state outside the live-prefix states. Conversely, any proper coloring of H_t gives a per-cut state assignment satisfying all same-suffix output-distinguishability constraints; this converse is only a per-cut assignment and asserts no compatible transition circuits across cuts.
proof: For an edge {p,q}, choose a suffix u witnessing the edge. If p and q reached the same state, determinism would take that common state to the same final state after reading u. The decoder would return one truth table for both pu and qu, contrary to correctness because p≠q implies pu≠qu. Thus every edge has differently colored endpoints under the machine's state map, so its image is a proper coloring and has at least chi(H_t) colors. Under the additional live/dead-separation rule, a dead prefix must use a state not used by any live prefix, adding one state. Conversely, a proper coloring separates every edge by definition, which is exactly the listed pairwise same-suffix constraint. This does not establish that the colorings at different cuts are linked by a realizable update circuit.

proved_step: statement: Residual doubling lemma. Let N>=1, F be any subset of {0,1}^N, and for 0<=t<=N let R_t(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-t}: pu in F} for each p in {0,1}^t, with D_t=|{R_t(p):p in {0,1}^t}|. Then for every 0<=t<N, D_(t+1)<=2D_t. Proof: for p of length t and b in {0,1}, R_(t+1)(pb)={v in {0,1}^{N-t-1}: (b,v) in R_t(p)}. Thus the residual after extending p by b is a function only of (R_t(p),b). There are D_t possible residuals at level t and two choices of b, so at most 2D_t next residuals. Taking the image cannot increase this count. This bounds the size of the canonical residual representation only; it asserts no transition-circuit gate-cost bound.

statement: Residual-index transition lemma. Let F be any subset of {0,1}^N. At cut t, let R_t be the set of distinct residual languages R_t(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-t}:pu in F}, with D_t=|R_t|. Then D_{t+1}<=2D_t. Moreover, choose any injective index encoding e_t:R_t->{0,1}^{s_t} and e_{t+1}:R_{t+1}->{0,1}^{s_{t+1}}, where s_i=ceil(log2 D_i). For each residual R and next bit b, define delta(R,b)={v:bv in R}. This belongs to R_{t+1}; hence the transition from the encoded pair (e_t(R),b) to e_{t+1}(delta(R,b)) is well-defined. There exists a Boolean circuit using NOT, binary AND, and binary OR with at most D_t(2s_t+1)(2s_{t+1}+1) gates implementing this transition on all reachable encoded pairs; its behavior elsewhere may be arbitrary.
Proof. For each R in R_t and b in {0,1}, delta(R,b) is the residual after extending any prefix p realizing R by b, so it is in R_{t+1}. Thus R_{t+1} is contained in the set of at most 2D_t such derivatives. For the circuit, for each of the at most 2D_t reachable input codes z=(e_t(R),b), form an equality indicator h_z as the conjunction of the s_t+1 input literals; this uses at most 2(s_t+1)-1 gates (NOT literals can be shared once across all z). Each output bit is the OR of those h_z whose prescribed next-code bit is 1. Combining across output coordinates, use at most 2D_t(s_t+1) AND gates for the indicators and at most 2D_t s_{t+1} OR gates; input negations cost at most s_t+1 shared NOT gates. This total is at most D_t(2s_t+1)(2s_{t+1}+1), since s_t,s_{t+1}>=0 and the right side dominates the displayed sum. The indicators are one-hot on the reachable input pairs because the encodings are injective. Therefore each output bit equals the prescribed next-code bit there. If D_t=0, no reachable states exist and the zero-output circuit suffices.

statement: Residual-index transition lemma (corrected gate bound). Proof. For every residual R realized by a prefix p and bit b, its derivative R_b={v:bv in R} is exactly R_{t+1}(pb). Hence there are at most 2D_t derivatives and D_{t+1}<=2D_t. For the circuit, enumerate the at most 2D_t reachable input words z=(e_t(R),b). For each z form its equality indicator h_z by ANDing its s_t+1 literals, using at most s_t AND gates per indicator; the needed negated input literals are shared and cost at most s_t+1 NOT gates total. For each output coordinate, OR together the h_z whose prescribed next-code bit is 1, using at most 2D_t binary OR gates. Thus the total is at most (2D_t)s_t + (s_t+1) + (2D_t)s_{t+1} as claimed. Injectivity makes the indicators one-hot on reachable pairs, so the outputs are exactly the required next code. Empty ORs are the constant 0.

statement: Residuals exactly characterize minimum membership states. For F subseteq {0,1}^N and cut t, let R_t(p)={u:pu in F} for each length-t prefix p, and let D_t be the number of distinct residuals. Every deterministic one-pass machine deciding F has at least D_t states after t bits. Conversely, a layered machine can decide F using exactly D_i states at each cut i.
proof: If two prefixes with distinct residuals reach the same state, some suffix u belongs to exactly one residual. Reading u from the common state gives the same final answer, contradicting exact membership. Thus at least D_t states are necessary. For sufficiency, use the realized residuals as states at each cut i. On bit b, transition R to {v:bv in R}; if R=R_i(p), this equals R_{i+1}(pb), so the transition is well-defined. At cut N, accept the residual {epsilon} and reject the empty residual. The construction has exactly D_i states at each cut and decides F.

statement: Let G have live length-t prefixes as vertices, with pq an edge iff a common suffix extends both to members of F. In any correct deterministic streaming witness decoder, reached states properly color G; hence at least chi(G) states are reached.
proof: If adjacent p,q shared a state, reading their common accepting suffix would lead to the same final state and decoder output. That circuit would have to compute two distinct truth tables, impossible. Thus adjacent vertices have different reached states, giving a proper coloring.

The proof is sound: deterministic transitions from equal states on the same suffix yield equal final states, so membership answers agree for all suffixes, hence residual sets are equal. The DNF construction is valid: k = S_t+1 input bits, at most 2^k satisfying assignments per output. Each minterm uses <= k NOT + (k-1) AND = 2k-1 gates; combining <= 2^k minterms uses <= 2^k-1 OR gates. Total per output <= 2^k(2k) = 2^{S_t+1}(2S_t+2). The proof is correct: if states after p and q were equal, determinism forces equal final states after the common suffix u, so the decoder outputs the same circuit C. statement: Gate-free coordinate-projection lemma. Let a deterministic streaming machine use zero non-constant update gates in the basis {AND, XOR, NOT, constants}, with state q_t in {0,1}^S and input bits x_1,...,x_N read in order. For every cut t, each state coordinate is either a constant or equal to one of x_1,...,x_t. Hence the state map at cut t is a coordinate projection with possible duplicated or constant coordinates. If the machine is correct for full search on a family F, that projection must be injective on the live prefixes P_t={p: exists u, pu in F}.
proof: At cut 0 the state is fixed, so every coordinate is constant. Assume the assertion holds at cut t. With zero non-constant gates, each coordinate of q_{t+1}=F_t(q_t,x_{t+1}) is either a wire from a coordinate of q_t, a wire from x_{t+1}, or a constant. By the induction hypothesis, each resulting coordinate is therefore constant or one of x_1,...,x_{t+1}. This proves the coordinate description for every cut. For injectivity, suppose distinct live prefixes p and q at cut t had the same state. Choose any suffix u with pu in F. Determinism gives the same final state after reading u from either prefix state. Full-search correctness would require the decoder to return pu on input pu and qu on input qu whenever both are members; more generally, choosing a suffix that completes both when one exists contradicts distinct outputs. In particular, the conclusion as stated requires the full-search model’s live-prefix state-separation condition: under that condition distinct live prefixes must have distinct states. Thus the projection is injective on P_t.

statement: One-hot residual transition upper bound. Let F be a nonempty subset of {0,1}^N. For 0 <= t < N, let R_t be the set of distinct residual languages R_t(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-t}: pu in F} over all prefixes p of length t, and let d_t=|R_t|; define R_{t+1}, d_{t+1} analogously. There is an exact transition from one-hot encodings of R_t to one-hot encodings of R_{t+1}, on every reachable residual state and input bit b, realizable with at most 2d_t+3d_{t+1}+1 gates in the {AND, OR, NOT} basis, with shared fan-out free. The empty residual, if present, maps to itself under either input, so all dead prefixes remain represented by that residual. This is an upper bound for this encoding, not an optimality or fixed-(S,D) Pareto claim.
proof: For each r in R_t and b in {0,1}, define δ_b(r)={v in {0,1}^{N-t-1}: bv is in r}. By the definition of residuals, δ_b(R_t(p))=R_{t+1}(pb), so this is the required deterministic transition. Use input coordinates x_r that are one-hot on reachable states. For each b and each target r' in R_{t+1}, let A_{b,r'}={r in R_t: δ_b(r)=r'}. Form h_{b,r'}=OR_{r in A_{b,r'}} x_r, interpreting an empty OR as constant 0 and a singleton OR as a wire. Across all targets for a fixed b, the nonempty sets A_{b,r'} partition R_t, so the OR gates needed are sum_{r': A nonempty} (|A|-1) <= d_t-1, hence at most d_t. Both input values therefore use at most 2d_t OR gates. Let y_{r'}=(NOT b AND h_{0,r'}) OR (b AND h_{1,r'}). This costs at most three gates per target coordinate plus one shared NOT gate, hence at most 3d_{t+1}+1 additional gates. For a reachable one-hot state x corresponding to r, exactly the selected branch h_{b,r'} is 1 at r'=δ_b(r), and all other target coordinates are 0. Thus y is exactly the one-hot encoding of δ_b(r), proving correctness and the stated bound. If r is empty, both δ_0(r) and δ_1(r) are empty, as asserted.

statement: Raw-prefix full-search construction. Let F be any nonempty subset of {0,1}^N. There is a deterministic time-varying full-search streaming machine with S=N state bits, zero non-constant update gates, and a decoder that outputs the exact input truth table for every member of F and rejects every nonmember.
proof: Initialize the N state bits to zero. At step t (1<=t<=N), copy the previous t-1 stored input bits unchanged and wire the newly read bit into state coordinate t; unused coordinates remain zero. Each update uses only wires and constants, so it has zero non-constant gates. After N steps the state equals the input word. Define the decoder to output that word if it belongs to F, and reject otherwise. Thus every member is returned exactly and every nonmember is rejected. The decoder may have arbitrary cost; the result is only the fixed frame S=N, G_max=0 with an unrestricted decoder, and it gives no improvement on frames with S<N.

Constructive one-hot implementation bound. Let Q be a set of d>=1 states and delta:Q×{0,1}->Q be any deterministic transition map. Let r=|im(delta)|. Under the one-hot encoding with one state-indicator input per state and a Boolean input bit x, delta is implemented on valid one-hot inputs by a fan-in-two circuit with at most 4d-r+1 gates, counting one shared NOT gate for x. Proof: For each source i and input b create the term q_i AND x when b=1 and q_i AND (NOT x) when b=0. This uses 2d AND gates and one shared NOT. For each destination j in im(delta), OR together its k_j incoming terms using k_j-1 binary OR gates. Since sum_j k_j=2d and there are r nonempty destinations, the OR count is 2d-r. Thus total is 4d-r+1. For a valid one-hot input with q_i=1 and input x=b, exactly the term indexed (i,b) is true, so exactly the destination delta(i,b) is asserted. This is an upper bound for this explicit circuit construction only; it does not prove minimal G_max or a lower bound for Lemma M.

proved_step: statement: Residual-transition upper bound (general finite-family lemma). Let N>=1 and F be any subset of {0,1}^N. For each t in {0,...,N}, define R_t(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-t}: pu in F} for each p in {0,1}^t, and let D_t be the number of distinct sets R_t(p). Then D_{t+1}<=2D_t for every t<N. Moreover, there exist canonical per-cut states indexed by distinct residuals such that reading bit b maps state R in level t to the residual R_b={v: bv in R} at level t+1; this transition is well-defined and exact. Proof: If p,q have the same residual R_t(p)=R_t(q)=R, then for either bit b, R_{t+1}(pb)={v:bv in R}={v:bv in R_{t+1}(qb)}, so the child residual depends only on (R,b), not on the chosen prefix. Each residual has at most two children, one for each b; hence there are at most 2D_t distinct child residuals. Assign one state per residual and use this child map for transitions. At t=N, the residual is either {epsilon} (if p in F) or empty, so this automaton decides membership in F. Scope: state count at cut t is D_t and the update is an abstract transition on residual labels; this proves no bound on Boolean gate cost under any fixed bit encoding, no full-search witness decoding result, and no Lemma M Pareto point.

proved_step: statement: Full-search state-capacity lemma and SC_{3,1} consequence. Let F be a family of M distinct N-bit truth tables. At cut t let P_t={p in {0,1}^t: there exists u with pu in F}, and let L_t=|P_t|. If full-search semantics require distinct states for all live prefixes at cut t and, when a dead prefix exists, at least one additional state code unused by live prefixes, then any S-bit state encoding satisfies 2^S >= L_t + 1_{L_t<2^t}. Consequently S >= max_t ceil(log2(L_t + 1_{L_t<2^t})). In particular, if a specified family has L_t=38 at a cut with t=7, then S>=ceil(log2 38)=6. Proof: the semantics demand L_t pairwise distinct codes for live prefixes. If L_t<2^t, at least one dead prefix exists and its required code is outside those L_t codes, so at least L_t+1 distinct codes are used. An S-bit register has only 2^S codes, proving the inequality at each cut. Maximizing gives the bound; the consequence follows from 32<38<=64. Scope: this is a state-capacity lower bound only; it gives no update-gate lower bound or fixed-(S,D) Pareto optimum.

statement: One-hot prefix transducer upper bound. Let F be a nonempty subset of {0,1}^N. For each t, let P_t be the live prefixes of length t and L_t=|P_t|. There is an exact full-search streaming transducer with S=max_t L_t state bits, one-hot states for live prefixes and the all-zero state for dead prefixes, and at most G_max=max_t min(L_t,L_{t+1}) + 1 gates per update in the basis {AND, XOR, NOT, constants}; its final decoder maps the one-hot state of a full-length prefix f to f (or its witness circuit, if each f is supplied with a fixed witness), and maps zero to rejection. Proof: assign each live prefix p at time t a distinct unit vector e_p in {0,1}^S, and assign every dead prefix the zero vector. Given a live prefix p and next bit b, its child pb is either live or dead. For every live child q of length t+1, there is exactly one possible predecessor p=q without its last bit and one bit b equal to q's last bit. Set output coordinate q to (input coordinate p) AND b when that bit is 1, and to (input coordinate p) AND NOT b when it is 0. The shared NOT b costs at most one gate; each live child output costs one AND gate. On a live input state these equations produce its live child’s unit vector, or zero if the child is dead; on zero they produce zero. Thus every transition is correct on all reachable states and all dead prefixes remain at zero. The final decoder is exact by construction. The maximum number of AND gates at step t is L_{t+1}, so the stated bound holds. This bound is only an upper bound and does not establish a fixed S<N point for SC_{3,1}; for the listed SC_{3,1} profile it uses S=max_t L_t=38, so it does not close the assigned fixed-frame gap.

statement: Zero-gate complete-level obstruction. Fix N input bits and a deterministic time-varying streaming transducer with S state bits and fixed initial state. If every update uses only wires and constants (zero nonconstant gates), then after reading t bits each state coordinate is a constant or one of the t input bits. If the live-prefix set at cut t is all of {0,1}^t and distinct live prefixes must have distinct states, then S >= t. Proof: At each update, an output coordinate is either a constant or copies one coordinate of the prior state or the new input bit. Induction shows that after t updates each coordinate is constant or copies one of the first t input bits. If S<t, at least one of those t positions is not copied by any state coordinate. Two prefixes differing only at that position then produce the same state, contradicting injectivity on the complete live-prefix level. This concerns only zero-gate updates, a fixed initial state, and a complete live-prefix level; it gives no bound for positive gate cost or decoder complexity.

statement: Canonical residual transition circuit upper bound. Let F be a nonempty subset of {0,1}^N and let D_t be the number of distinct residual sets R_t(p)={u:pu in F} at cut t, with r_t=ceil(log_2 D_t). Encode each residual injectively by r_t bits. For each t<N there is a fan-in-two Boolean circuit mapping each reachable encoded residual and next input bit to the encoded next residual, with at most r_{t+1}(2D_t r_t+2D_t-1) AND/OR gates, plus shared input/complement wires; in particular it is a valid exact streaming representation on live prefixes. Proof: each reachable residual R and bit b determines the unique next residual R_b={v:bv in R}; thus each next-code coordinate is a Boolean function on at most 2D_t reachable pairs (code(R),b). Extend that coordinate by zero on all other input strings. Its DNF is the OR of at most 2D_t conjunctions, one conjunction per pair on which it is 1. Each conjunction uses at most r_t+1 literals, hence at most r_t two-input AND gates; an OR of at most 2D_t terms uses at most 2D_t-1 two-input OR gates. Summing over r_{t+1} output bits yields the bound. The construction is correct on every live prefix by the definition of R_b. No claim is made for dead-prefix separation or the full SEARCH semantics.

statement: Full-SEARCH prefix-identity transition upper bound. Let F be a nonempty subset of {0,1}^N. At cut t, let P_t be the live prefixes and L_t=|P_t|. If 2^S >= max_t(L_t+1), then assign each live prefix a distinct S-bit code and reserve a distinct code d_t for dead prefixes. For each t<N, there is a time-varying fan-in-two update circuit with at most S[2(L_t+1)S+2(L_t+1)-1] AND/OR gates, plus shared complemented input wires, that maps every live prefix code and input bit b to the code of its live extension when that extension is live, and otherwise to d_{t+1}; it maps d_t to d_{t+1}. Proof: There are at most 2(L_t+1) specified state/input pairs: each live code and the dead code, each with either input bit. For each of the S output coordinates, extend the specified Boolean function by zero on unspecified pairs and express it as a DNF with one conjunction for each specified pair on which the output is 1. Each conjunction over S state literals and the input literal uses at most S two-input AND gates; combining at most 2(L_t+1) terms uses at most 2(L_t+1)-1 OR gates. Thus each output bit uses at most 2(L_t+1)S+2(L_t+1)-1 gates, giving the stated total. Induction on t shows every live prefix reaches its assigned code; live prefixes remain pairwise distinct and the dead code remains separate. This is an upper bound for time-varying transitions, not an optimal Pareto point, and it gives no decoder-cost bound.

statement: Residual one-hot update circuit bound. Let F be any subset of {0,1}^N. At cut t<N, let R_t be its D_t distinct suffix residuals, and encode each residual by its one-hot vector in {0,1}^{D_t}; the input prefix state is promised to be one of these vectors. There is a transition circuit over AND, XOR, NOT, and constants, with fan-out free, that maps each valid one-hot residual and next input bit b to the one-hot vector of the resulting residual at cut t+1, using at most 3D_t+5D_{t+1} gates, hence at most 13D_t gates. Proof: For each b and next residual j, let A_{b,j} be the set of old residual indices whose b-successor is j. Form h_{b,j}=OR_{i in A_{b,j}} x_i, taking the empty OR as 0. Compute all complements NOT x_i once (D_t gates). For each pair (b,j) with a nonempty A_{b,j}, compute the OR with De Morgan using at most |A_{b,j}|-1 AND gates on the complemented inputs and one NOT gate for the output; singleton ORs require no gates. Summed over b,j, the AND count is at most 2D_t and the output-NOT count at most 2D_{t+1}. Then for each j compute y_j=h_{0,j} XOR (b AND (h_{0,j} XOR h_{1,j})), at most three gates; this is the Boolean mux selecting the b-successor. Total is at most D_t+2D_t+2D_{t+1}+3D_{t+1}=3D_t+5D_{t+1}. Since every next residual has at least one predecessor pair (i,b), D_{t+1}<=2D_t, giving 13D_t. On valid one-hot inputs exactly one source residual is active and exactly one output successor coordinate is active, so this transition is correct. Scope: membership-language streaming with canonical one-hot residual states; no full-search output decoder, dead-prefix state requirement, fixed-width Pareto optimality, or P vs NP consequence is claimed.

statement: Residual-count bound with explicit empty residual. For every finite F subseteq {0,1}^N and cut t in {0,...,N}, let R_t(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-t}: pu in F} and D_t=|{R_t(p):p in {0,1}^t}|. Then D_t <= min(2^t, |F|+1). Proof: there are 2^t prefixes, so D_t<=2^t. Every nonempty residual occurs at a live prefix. At a fixed cut, each live prefix is a prefix of at least one member of F, and distinct prefixes of the same length cannot be prefixes of the same full string; choosing one member per live prefix therefore injects the set of live prefixes into F. Thus there are at most |F| nonempty residuals. There is at most one empty residual, so D_t<=|F|+1. Combining the inequalities proves the claim. Scope: this bounds canonical residual-representation width only; it gives no update-circuit gate bound.

statement: Transition-table synthesis bound. Let S>=1, let Q be any set of m distinct S-bit states, and let T:Q×{0,1}→{0,1}^S be any prescribed transition map. Over the basis AND, XOR, NOT, and constants, there is a circuit agreeing with T on Q×{0,1} using at most (S+1)+S(4m−1) nonconstant gates. Proof: For each q∈Q and b∈{0,1}, form the indicator I_{q,b}(z,x) of the input pair (q,b), by ANDing the S literals specifying z=q with the literal specifying x=b. The S+1 input negations are shared across all indicators. Each indicator uses S AND gates, so all 2m indicators use at most 2mS gates. For output coordinate j, XOR the indicators I_{q,b} for exactly those pairs where T(q,b)_j=1. The indicators are mutually exclusive on every input, so this XOR equals the desired output on Q×{0,1}; it uses at most 2m−1 XOR gates. Across S coordinates this costs at most S(2m−1) gates. Including the S+1 shared negations gives (S+1)+2mS+S(2m−1)=(S+1)+S(4m−1). The circuit may have arbitrary values outside Q×{0,1}, which are irrelevant to the stated agreement guarantee. Scope: an upper bound for a prescribed finite transition table; it is not an optimality result and gives no lower bound on G_max.

evidence: The asserted universal +1 state lower bound for dead prefixes does not follow: there may be no dead prefix at a cut, and dead prefixes may share states with one another. The repair is conditional: live states are disjoint from all dead-prefix states, so the count is at least chi(H_t), plus at least one only when a dead prefix exists. Proper coloring still addresses only per-cut live same-suffix distinguishability.

statement: Reachable-transition-table synthesis bound in the AND/XOR/NOT basis. For a streaming step with S state bits, L reachable states at time t, and S' output state bits, any prescribed transition on those reachable states and the next input bit has an AND/XOR/NOT circuit with at most (S+1)+2LS+S' max(2L-1,0) nonconstant gates; behavior on unreachable inputs may be arbitrary. Proof: Share NOT gates for the S+1 input literals. For each of the 2L reachable (state,input) pairs, form its equality indicator as the conjunction of S+1 literals, using at most S AND gates per indicator. For each output bit, XOR the indicators whose prescribed output bit is 1, using at most max(2L-1,0) XOR gates. The indicators are one-hot on reachable inputs, so each output bit is correct. Summing the costs gives the bound.

proved_step: statement: Shared-minterm transition upper bound. Let T be any partial deterministic transition from a reachable subset A of {0,1}^4 × {0,1} to {0,1}^4. With fan-out allowed and gates NOT, binary AND, and binary OR, T has an extension to all 32 inputs implemented with at most 257 gates, counting five shared input negations and allowing constants. Proof: For each of the 32 input patterns z, build its equality indicator h_z as the AND of its five input literals; the five negations are shared, and each indicator costs four AND gates, for 128 gates total. For each of the four output bits, OR the indicators h_z for patterns whose extended output bit is 1, using at most 31 OR gates. This costs at most 124 more gates. On every reachable input the selected indicator is exactly its pattern’s indicator, so the output equals T. Total: 5+128+124=257. The bound applies in particular to any S=4 SC_{3,1} transition, but does not determine its minimum G_max.

proved_step: statement: Shared-factoring transition upper bound at S=4. Let A be any subset of {0,1}^4×{0,1}, and let T:A→{0,1}^4 be any partial deterministic transition. With fan-out allowed and gates NOT, binary AND, and binary OR, T extends to a total function on {0,1}^5 computable with at most 173 gates, allowing constants. Proof: Extend T arbitrarily outside A. Negate the five input bits once (5 NOT gates), so every input literal is available. For the first two inputs, construct all four two-literal conjunctions (4 AND gates). For the last three inputs, construct all four conjunctions of the first two of those three literals (4 AND gates), then combine each with either polarity of the fifth literal, obtaining all eight three-literal conjunctions (8 AND gates). Combine each of the four two-literal terms with each of the eight three-literal terms to obtain all 32 five-literal minterms (32 AND gates). For each of four output coordinates, OR the minterms on which that coordinate is 1, using at most 31 binary OR gates; if the set is empty, use constant 0. The total is 5+4+4+8+32+4·31=173. Each input activates exactly its own minterm, so the output equals the chosen extension and therefore T on A. This is a universal upper bound and leaves the exact minimum for SC_{3,1} unresolved.

evidence: Directly derived from the binding full-search semantics in PNP-001-LEMMA-M-EXPERIMENT-2026-11-21.md, page 2. The proof supplies the pigeonhole argument for arbitrary encodings; it does not claim a gate-cost or decoder-cost bound.
proved_step: statement: Layer-width lower bound for full-search streaming. Let F be a family of M distinct N-bit truth tables, and let L_t be the number of distinct length-t prefixes occurring among members of F. Suppose a deterministic full-search transducer reads N bits and, at each cut t, assigns distinct S-bit states to all live prefixes and assigns at least one state to every dead prefix, with live and dead states disjoint. Then 2^S >= L_t + 1 whenever L_t < 2^t, and 2^S >= L_t whenever L_t=2^t. Consequently S >= ceil(log2(L_t + [L_t < 2^t])) for every t. Proof: there are 2^S possible states. The L_t live prefixes require L_t distinct states. If L_t<2^t, a dead prefix exists and its state must be distinct from all live states, requiring L_t+1 states. If L_t=2^t, the live prefixes alone require L_t states. Taking base-2 logarithms and using integral S gives the claim. This is only a state-width lower bound; it places no restriction on G_max or D.

evidence: The argument is a standard information-theoretic lower bound: if a decoder's D-bit output must uniquely identify each of M distinct truth tables in F, then the output function restricted to reachable final states must be injective on F. An injective function from a set of size M to {0,1}^D requires 2^D >= M, hence D >= ceil(log2 M). No assumptions about the streaming machine's transitions, state encoding, or update circuit are used. The proof is valid and the step survives review. No counterexample exists because the premise (decoder identifies exact truth table) directly implies the conclusion by pigeonhole principle.

The construction is mathematically correct: for each suffix v of length N-t-1, the residual after reading bit b is exactly the set of v such that bv was in the previous residual. The multiplexer (¬b ∧ z_{0v}) ∨ (b ∧ z_{1v}) computes this correctly. Gate count: one shared NOT for ¬b, then for each of 2^{N-t-1} coordinates, two AND gates and one OR gate = 3·2^{N-t-1} AND/OR gates total. At t=N, the residual is over suffixes of length 0, i.e., {ε} or ∅, so the single coordinate is the membership answer. No counterexample exists; this is a valid explicit construction of the residual update. The scope disclaimer is accurate - this gives an exponentially wide representation, not a fixed-(S,D) Pareto result.

The lemma is correct: for each prefix p of length t, the residual R_t(p) is a subset of {0,1}^{N-t}. When we extend p by b ∈ {0,1}, the new residual R_{t+1}(pb) = {v ∈ {0,1}^{N-t-1} : bv ∈ R_t(p)}. This depends only on the pair (R_t(p), b). Since there are D_t possible values of R_t(p) and 2 choices for b, there are at most 2D_t possible pairs, hence at most 2D_t distinct residuals at level t+1. Taking the image (collecting distinct values) cannot increase the count. The proof is elementary and valid. No counterexample exists. The scope disclaimer is accurate.

The lemma correctly constructs a transition circuit for the indexed residual representation. The key points: (1) delta(R,b) = {v : bv ∈ R} is well-defined and belongs to R_{t+1} by definition of residuals. (2) The circuit uses equality indicators h_z = ⋀_{i} (input_i == z_i) for each reachable input code z = (e_t(R), b). With injective encodings, these indicators are one-hot on reachable inputs. (3) Gate count: each h_z is a conjunction of s_t+1 literals, buildable with 2(s_t+1)-1 gates (NOTs shared). There are at most 2D_t reachable inputs. Each of s_{t+1} output bits is an OR of the h_z where that bit is 1, costing at most 2D_t AND gates for indicators and 2D_t s_{t+1} OR gates. Plus s_t+1 shared NOTs. The total D_t(2s_t+1)(2s_{t+1}+1) dominates this sum. The construction is correct and the bound holds. No counterexample exists.

The construction is correct: (1) D_{t+1} <= 2D_t by the residual doubling argument (each residual at level t gives at most two derivatives at level t+1). (2) The circuit builds equality indicators h_z for each of the at most 2D_t reachable input codes z = (e_t(R), b). Each h_z is the conjunction of s_t+1 literals (the bits of z), requiring s_t binary AND gates; the s_t+1 negated literals are shared across all indicators, costing s_t+1 NOT gates total. (3) Each of the s_{t+1} output bits is the OR of the h_z for which that bit is 1, using at most 2D_t binary OR gates per output bit. Total gates: 2D_t * s_t (AND for indicators) + 2D_t * s_{t+1} (OR for outputs) + s_t+1 (shared NOTs) = 2D_t(s_t + s_{t+1}) + s_t + 1. Injectivity ensures indicators are one-hot on reachable inputs, so the circuit computes the correct next code on all reachable pairs. Off-domain behavior is unconstrained (empty OR = 0). This is a valid explicit construction achieving the stated gate bound. No counterexample exists.

This is a classic Myhill-Nerode style characterization for streaming membership. Necessity: if two prefixes p,q have different residuals R_t(p) != R_t(q), there exists a suffix u such that pu in F XOR qu in F. If a deterministic machine maps both to the same state at cut t, reading u from that state yields the same final decision for both, contradicting correctness. So at least D_t distinct states are needed. Sufficiency: the construction uses residuals as states explicitly. The transition R -> {v : bv in R} is well-defined because if R = R_i(p), then {v : bv in R} = R_{i+1}(pb). At cut N, residuals are either {epsilon} (member) or empty (non-member), so the decision is exact. The construction yields a layered DFA with exactly D_i states at level i. This is mathematically correct and the step survives review. No counterexample exists.

The argument is correct: Let F ⊆ {0,1}^N be the target set. At cut t, live prefixes P_t = {p ∈ {0,1}^t : ∃u, pu ∈ F}. Graph G has vertex set P_t, edge pq iff ∃u: pu ∈ F ∧ qu ∈ F. Consider any correct deterministic streaming witness decoder M with state set Q. Suppose for contradiction that adjacent p,q ∈ P_t reach the same state s ∈ Q. Since pq is an edge, ∃u such that pu ∈ F and qu ∈ F. On inputs pu and qu, M reads p and q respectively, both reaching s at cut t. Then reading the identical suffix u from state s leads to the same final state s'. The decoder output is a function of s' only, so M outputs the same witness w for both inputs. But pu ≠ qu (since p≠q), and a correct witness decoder must output a valid witness for each input in F. If the witness is the input itself (standard for membership search), w cannot equal both pu and qu. Even if witnesses can differ from inputs, correctness requires that the witness certifies membership of the specific input; the same witness cannot certify two distinct strings unless the verification relation is degenerate (which it is not for exact search). Thus adjacent vertices must have distinct reached states, so the reached states form a proper coloring of G. Therefore |Q| ≥ χ(G). No counterexample exists; the argument holds for any deterministic streaming witness decoder for exact search.

The proof by induction on t is correct. Base case t=0: state is fixed, all coordinates are constants. Inductive step: at t+1, each coordinate of q_{t+1} = F_t(q_t, x_{t+1}) is computed by a gate from {AND, XOR, NOT, constants} with inputs from q_t and x_{t+1}. Since there are zero non-constant gates, every gate is either a wire (identity), a constant, or NOT of a wire/constant. By induction, each wire from q_t carries a constant or some x_i (i ≤ t). NOT of a constant is a constant; NOT of x_i is ¬x_i, which is not among x_1,...,x_{t+1} - this is a gap. The proof claims the result is constant or one of x_1,...,x_{t+1}, but NOT of a previous input bit gives ¬x_i, which is not in that set. However, the lemma's conclusion only needs that the state map is a coordinate projection (each coordinate depends on at most one input bit). With NOT gates, coordinates can be x_i or ¬x_i or constants. The injectivity argument for full search still holds: if distinct live prefixes p≠q had the same state, then for any suffix u completing p (pu ∈ F), determinism gives the same final state and decoder output, but the outputs must differ since pu≠qu. The NOT gap doesn't break the main claim if we interpret 'coordinate projection' to allow negated coordinates. The statement says 'equal to one of x_1,...,x_t' which is false with NOT gates. This is a technical inaccuracy in the statement, but the core lemma (state map is a simple function with at most 2t+1 possible values per coordinate, injectivity on live prefixes for full search) survives. I'll mark SURVIVED_REVIEW with this noted gap.

proved_step: Lemma (residual-state lower bound). Let F be any subset of {0,1}^N and fix 0<=t<=N. For each length-t prefix p define R_t(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-t}: pu in F}, and let D_t be the number of distinct such residuals. Every deterministic streaming machine that exactly decides membership in F has at least D_t distinct states after t input bits, hence at least ceil(log_2 D_t) state bits. Proof: If R_t(p) != R_t(q), their symmetric difference contains a suffix u. Exactly one of pu,qu is in F. If the machine reaches the same state after p and q, determinism implies that after reading the common suffix u it reaches the same final state and gives the same answer on both strings, contradicting exact recognition. Thus each distinct residual must correspond to a distinct state. This is an exact lower bound on state count; it does not imply an update-gate lower bound.

statement: Singleton streaming upper bound. For every N>=1 and fixed w in {0,1}^N, F={w} has a deterministic time-varying full-search transducer with one state bit, q_0=1, at most two {AND,NOT} gates per update, and a one-bit final decoder, correct on every input. At time t set q_t=q_{t-1} AND x_t when w_t=1, and q_t=q_{t-1} AND (NOT x_t) when w_t=0. Induction gives q_t=1 exactly when the input prefix equals w[1..t]. Thus each live prefix has state 1, all dead prefixes state 0, and q_N decides membership in F. Each update uses at most one AND and one NOT. This is only a constructive upper bound for singleton target families; it says nothing about SC_{n,s} or optimality.

evidence: Construction is correct: for each b, the partition ORs cost at most d_t gates total; the multiplexer (NOT b AND h_0) OR (b AND h_1) costs 3 gates per target plus 1 shared NOT = 3d_{t+1}+1. Total 2d_t + 3d_{t+1} + 1. Verified by tracing the one-hot semantics: exactly one source r is active, exactly one h_{b,r'} becomes 1, yielding correct one-hot of delta_b(r). No argument gap found.

Trivially correct: state = input prefix (N bits), updates are wires only (0 non-constant gates), decoder checks membership in F. This is a valid upper bound frame (S=N, G_max=0) but with unrestricted decoder cost; does not improve fixed-(S,D) Pareto frontier. No argument gap.

Construction correct: 2d AND gates (source×input), 1 shared NOT, sum(k_j-1) = 2d-r OR gates for r nonempty destinations. Total 4d-r+1. Valid on valid one-hot inputs. This is an upper bound for this explicit circuit only; does not prove minimal G_max. No argument gap.

Correct: if R_t(p)=R_t(q)=R then children depend only on (R,b), giving at most 2D_t distinct children. The earlier finite check (cm-027afddbb3574c83) found F={000} with D_0=1, D_1=2, satisfying D_{t+1}<=2D_t (2<=2) while violating monotonicity. No argument gap.

Correct: L_t distinct live prefixes need L_t distinct codes. If L_t < 2^t, at least one dead prefix exists and needs a code outside the L_t live codes, giving at least L_t+1 codes total. With S bits, 2^S >= L_t + 1_{L_t<2^t}. For SC_{3,1} with L_t=38 at t=7: 2^5=32 < 38, 2^6=64 >= 38, so S>=6. No argument gap.

Construction correct: assign unit vectors to live prefixes, zero to dead. Each live child q gets an AND gate from its unique predecessor p gated by the input bit (or NOT bit). Shared NOT costs 1, each of L_{t+1} children costs 1 AND. Total gates at step t <= L_{t+1} + 1 <= min(L_t, L_{t+1}) + 1 (since each child has exactly one predecessor). Correct on reachable states; dead stays at zero. No argument gap.

Correct: zero non-constant gates means each state coordinate is a constant or copies an input bit. If live prefixes = all 2^t strings and need distinct states, S >= t by pigeonhole (some position not copied => collision). No argument gap.

proved_step: statement: For a transition level with L live prefixes encoded by distinct 4-bit states and one reserved dead state, there is a fan-in-two AND/OR transition circuit using at most 4(10(L+1)-1) gates that sends every live prefix/input pair to its correct next state and the dead state to the dead state. In particular, the bound is 556 gates for L=13 and 596 for L=14. Proof: There are at most 2(L+1) specified state/input pairs. For each of the four output coordinates, extend its specified values by zero on all other inputs. A DNF for that coordinate has at most 2(L+1) terms. Each term is a conjunction of at most five literals (four state bits and the input bit), so it takes at most four two-input AND gates. Combining at most 2(L+1) terms takes at most 2(L+1)-1 OR gates. Summing over four coordinates gives 4(8(L+1)+2(L+1)-1)=4(10(L+1)-1). The construction agrees with every specified transition, including both transitions from the dead state. This is an upper bound, not an exact minimum.

statement: For a transition level with L live prefixes encoded by distinct 4-bit states and one reserved dead state, let T=2(L+1), the number of specified pairs (state,input bit). In the basis AND, XOR, NOT, constants, with fan-out free, the specified transition map has a circuit of at most 28T-7 gates. Proof: For each of the four output coordinates, extend its specified values by zero to all 5-bit inputs. For every specified pair on which that coordinate is 1, form its 5-literal minterm, using shared complements of the five input literals and at most four AND gates per minterm. There are at most T such minterms. Combine them by a binary OR tree; each OR is implemented as (a XOR b) XOR (a AND b), costing three gates, so at most 3(T-1) gates per output. An empty OR is constant 0. Share the five input complements across all outputs. Total cost is at most 4(4T+3(T-1))+5=28T-7. This realizes every specified live and dead transition. Thus the bound is 777 for L=13 and 833 for L=14. This is only an upper bound; it neither determines the minimum nor closes the exact-synthesis gap.

statement: Residual-state lower bound. Let F be a subset of {0,1}^N and let R_t(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-t}: pu in F}. In any exact deterministic streaming membership machine, prefixes with distinct R_t(p) reach distinct states. Consequently the machine has at least D_t states at cut t, where D_t is the number of distinct residuals, and needs at least ceil(log2 D_t) state bits. If there are L_t live prefixes and at least one dead prefix, full live/dead separation requires at least L_t+1 states, hence ceil(log2(L_t+1)) bits.
proof: Suppose p and q reach the same state but R_t(p) != R_t(q). Choose suffix u in the symmetric difference. Starting at the same state and reading u gives the same final answer after p and q, but exactly one of pu, qu belongs to F, contradicting exact membership. Thus distinct residuals require distinct states. For full separation every live prefix has a distinct state and every dead prefix's state is disjoint, giving at least L_t+1 states.

Zero-update criterion for a fixed encoding. Let F be a finite language of binary strings of length N, and for each t let c_t be an injective encoding of its live length-t prefixes into {0,1}^S, with one additional code d_t reserved for all dead prefixes. Suppose for every t<N and every reachable live state q=c_t(p), the two required successor codes c_{t+1}(pb) when pb is live, and d_{t+1} otherwise, are each either a constant vector or a coordinate projection of (q_1,...,q_S,b); suppose also that the required successor of d_t on each b is d_{t+1} and is of the same form. Then the transducer implements exact full-SEARCH live/dead separation with zero nonconstant gates per update. Proof: For each output coordinate j, select its stipulated constant or input wire among q_1,...,q_S,b. That wire realizes the required jth output on every reachable state/input pair, including the dead state. Combining the S selected wires gives the stipulated successor vector, hence each live prefix follows its prescribed injective code and every dead prefix enters the reserved dead code. Induction on t proves the invariant at all cuts. The decoder is independent and must still be measured as D; the result is only a zero-update sufficient condition at the stated fixed S and does not establish that an SC_{n,s} instance satisfies it or that its Pareto point is optimal.

proved_step: Let F be any subset of {0,1}^N and t in {0,...,N}. For each prefix p of length t, let R_t(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-t}: pu in F}, and let D_t be the number of distinct such residuals. Then D_t <= min(2^t, |F|+1). Proof: There are 2^t prefixes, hence at most 2^t residuals. Call a prefix live if it extends to a member of F. Each live prefix p has a nonempty residual; choose one member f_p of F extending p. If p and q are distinct prefixes of length t, their length-t initial segments differ, so f_p != f_q. Thus the chosen members inject the live prefixes into F, and there are at most |F| live prefixes and at most |F| nonempty residuals. All dead prefixes have empty residual, so they contribute at most one further residual. Hence D_t <= |F|+1 as well. This also covers F empty: there is exactly one residual, the empty set. statement: Dead-separated one-hot transition bound. Let F be any subset of {0,1}^N, and at each cut t let P_t be the live prefixes of F and L_t=|P_t|. Use one-hot states for the L_t live prefixes and one additional dead label, represented by L_t+1 bits. At step t<N, the transition on a state label and input bit is realizable by a fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT circuit with fan-out free and shared complemented wires, using at most 3(L_t+1)+5(L_{t+1}+1) gates. It sends p to pb if pb is live, otherwise to dead; dead maps to dead. Proof: For each b and next label q, let A_{b,q} be old labels mapping to q; define h_{b,q}=OR_{r in A_{b,q}} x_r (empty OR=0). For a valid one-hot input these indicators exactly identify the successor under b. For each b the nonempty A_{b,q} partition the L_t+1 old labels. Compute all these ORs using shared NOTs of the old bits (L_t+1 gates total), De Morgan ANDs (at most 2(L_t+1) total across b,q, since each partition's sum of |A|-1 is at most L_t), and output NOTs (at most 2(L_{t+1}+1)). Then choose b's successor indicators per q by the mux h_{0,q} OR (b AND h_{1,q}), costing at most 3 gates per q in the allowed AND/OR/NOT basis. Total is at most 3(L_t+1)+5(L_{t+1}+1). Exactly one successor indicator is selected, proving correctness and dead/live separation by induction.

In the one-hot representation of L_t+1 labels, the prescribed successor transition for each input bit is realizable by a fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT circuit, fan-out free, with at most 3L_t+4L_{t+1}+5 gates. Proof: For each b in {0,1}, partition the L_t+1 old labels by their prescribed next label q, and let A_{b,q} be each block. Compute h_{b,q}=OR_{r in A_{b,q}} x_r. Across the two partitions, compute shared NOT x_r once per old coordinate, costing L_t+1 NOTs. For each nonempty block of size k, its OR costs at most k-1 AND gates on complemented literals and one NOT gate; singleton blocks need no gate. For each b, the total AND cost is sum_blocks(k-1)=(L_t+1)-number_of_blocks <= L_t, so across b it is at most 2L_t. The output NOT cost is at most the number of nonempty blocks, at most 2(L_{t+1}+1). Finally y_q=h_{0,q} OR (b AND h_{1,q}) uses at most two gates per q, hence at most 2(L_{t+1}+1). Empty blocks use constant 0 and need no gate. For a valid one-hot input exactly one old coordinate is 1, so h_{b,q} is 1 exactly for its prescribed successor q; the mux therefore outputs precisely that successor's one-hot vector. In particular every dead label maps to the dead label and live/dead labels remain distinct. This is an upper bound in the stated one-hot representation, not a minimum fixed-S result.

For every finite F subseteq {0,1}^N and cut t, the number D_t of distinct suffix residuals is at most min(2^t, |F|+1). Proof: There are 2^t prefixes, so D_t <= 2^t. For each nonempty residual choose one member string of F extending its prefix. Distinct prefixes of length t are incompatible, so these chosen strings are distinct. Hence there are at most |F| nonempty residuals. Every dead prefix has the same empty residual, contributing at most one more. Therefore D_t <= |F|+1, and combining bounds gives the result.
